label: MODEL_DERIVED — architecture analysis with engineering-estimated response times; not validated

architectures.name: Pressure-relief bypass
architectures.description: Spring-loaded bypass valve that opens when differential pressure exceeds 15 mmHg, shunting CSF directly past the membrane to the venous outflow
architectures.worst_case: Spring fatigue after 5 years; valve may open at lower threshold or fail to open
architectures.failure_of_failure: Redundant second spring; if both fail, ICP rises but patient presents with headache (detectable)
architectures.modeled_safety_margin: PASS — bypass opens well below ICP_max_safe (20 mmHg)
architectures.complexity: MEDIUM — requires precision spring + valve seat

architectures.name: Membrane-bypass geometry
architectures.description: Membrane sleeve has axial slits that are normally closed by elastic preload; under high pressure, slits open to allow flow past the membrane
architectures.failure_mode: Slits fail to open (material creep, calcification)
architectures.trigger: dP > 18 mmHg (higher than FS1 — elastic opening requires more pressure)
architectures.worst_case: Slits permanently open (material yield) — membrane bypassed permanently, no retention
architectures.failure_of_failure: If slits yield, retention is lost but drainage preserved (trade-off: retention vs. drainage)
architectures.modeled_safety_margin: MARGINAL — higher trigger pressure, slower response
architectures.complexity: LOW — no moving parts beyond elastic deformation

architectures.name: Redundant drainage path
architectures.description: Second parallel drainage channel without membrane, normally closed by a dissolvable plug; if ICP rises, plug dissolves over hours, opening the parallel path
architectures.worst_case: Plug fails to dissolve (wrong CSF pH); ICP rises acutely
architectures.failure_of_failure: If plug fails, patient presents with acute hydrocephalus (symptomatic, requires intervention)
architectures.modeled_safety_margin: FAIL for acute occlusion — 2-hour response too slow
architectures.complexity: HIGH — requires biocompatible dissolvable material with controlled dissolution rate

selection.rationale: FS1 has the lowest trigger threshold (15 mmHg), fastest response (0.1s), highest residual flow (0.35 mL/min = full drainage), and acceptable failure-of-failure mode (symptomatic headache). FS2 is marginal (higher trigger, slower). FS3 fails for acute occlusion (2-hour response too slow). FS1 is selected as the primary fail-safe.
selection.fs3_rejected_reason: 2-hour response time is unacceptable for acute thrombus occlusion
selection.engineering_gate: PASS (with FS1) — but requires physical validation of spring fatigue life

honest_caveats: Response times are engineering estimates, not measured
Spring fatigue life (FS1) requires accelerated aging testing
Elastomer creep (FS2) requires chronic material testing
Dissolvable plug (FS3) requires novel material development
All architectures require chronic in vivo validation
